brief.topic: A Gentle Curve Shares a Force

s01: A rope wrapped around a wooden post can hold more than the same rope hanging freely.
The post contributes friction all along the contact.
Imagine the rope just about to slip toward the load.
We compare the larger load-side tension with the smaller holding tension.
More wrap allows a larger ratio between them.
Here is the total wrap angle laid along a line.
At the slipping threshold, each equal extra angle multiplies the allowed tension ratio by the same factor.
This happens because a tighter part of the rope presses harder against the post.
For one illustrative friction coefficient, a full turn allows a ratio of about three and a half.
Two turns allow about twelve, because that factor multiplies again.
The ideal capstan equation expresses this exponential growth.
Below the slipping threshold, friction need not reach its maximum.
Real rope stiffness and changing surface conditions also matter.
This is a model of a flexible rope with uniform friction.
A gentle curve can change how a force is shared.

scenes.narration:
A rope wrapped around a wooden post can hold more than the same rope hanging freely. The post contributes friction all along the contact.

Imagine the rope just about to slip toward the load. We compare the larger load-side tension with the smaller holding tension. More wrap allows a larger ratio between them.

Here is the total wrap angle laid along a line. At the slipping threshold, each equal extra angle multiplies the allowed tension ratio by the same factor. This happens because a tighter part of the rope presses harder against the post.

For one illustrative friction coefficient, a full turn allows a ratio of about three and a half. Two turns allow about twelve, because that factor multiplies again. The ideal capstan equation expresses this exponential growth.

Below the slipping threshold, friction need not reach its maximum. Real rope stiffness and changing surface conditions also matter. This is a model of a flexible rope with uniform friction. A gentle curve can change how a force is shared.
